42.0.s.en: (1) Jacob sends his sons to Egypt

42.0.0.en: Jacob heard that there was grain in Egypt, perhaps from the merchants who traveled to Egypt. He and his household were suffering from the famine that covered the whole land of Canaan, so he said to his sons, why do you stand bewildered before the problem of hunger, and he asked them to go down to Egypt to buy grain.

42.0.1.en: When a problem meets you, do not stand bewildered and helpless before it, but seek God and think of the solution. If you do not know, ask the counsel of those you trust, and do what you can do, and God will complete it and solve the problem, for He is able to do all things.

42.1.0.en: Jacob sent his ten sons to Egypt to buy grain, but he did not send his son Benjamin with them because of his young age and because he feared for him lest harm befall him like his brother Joseph.

42.2.0.en: People came from all the countries surrounding Egypt to buy grain from it, and among them the ten brothers of Joseph arrived. Joseph himself oversaw the selling in the eastern storehouses of Egypt, for the following reasons:

42.2.1.en: 1- To examine the strangers himself so that they would not cause trouble in the country, for most of the attacks on Egypt came from the east.

42.2.2.en: 2- To see his brothers, who might come, or to hear news of them from those who lived near them.

42.2.3.en: So when Joseph's brothers arrived and saw him, they did not recognize him, because of his great appearance and because more than twenty years had passed since their separation from him, in addition to the fact that he spoke the ancient Egyptian language and his name had also changed. So they bowed down before him with respect and reverence. Thus the old dreams of Joseph, from when he was in his father's house, were fulfilled in the bowing down of his brothers to him.

42.3.0.en: Joseph recognized his brothers and rejoiced greatly at seeing them, but they did not recognize him. He pretended not to know them, remembered his old dreams, then spoke to them harshly and did not reveal his identity to them, because he found it an opportunity to call them to repent of their old sins, which were envy, jealousy, and the vengeance they had done to him. He accused them of not wanting to buy grain but of being spies from a far country who wanted to see the weakness of Egypt so that they could attack it, and of taking the buying of grain as a deception and pretense. But they said that they were from Canaan and had come to buy grain.

42.3.1.en: Trust in God's promises to you in the Holy Bible. However long they are delayed, they must be fulfilled. And do not be troubled during afflictions, for they are temporary and prepare the way for you toward blessing, success, and greatness.

42.4.0.en: Joseph began his investigation of his brothers and questioned them as those accused of espionage, which is a grave crime. They tried to defend themselves and explained their circumstances: that they were the sons of one man, that they had a brother who was missing, and that the youngest was with their father in Canaan. This was what Joseph wanted to know, that is, to be reassured about his father and his brother Benjamin and about all their circumstances. But he still insisted on his harshness and on accusing them of espionage, until they should repent.

42.4.1.en: Be firm with those who err, and you may punish them with one aim only, their repentance, and not out of personal vengeance against them.

42.5.0.en: Joseph insisted on accusing them of espionage, but he gave them one chance to escape punishment: that one of them should go and bring their youngest brother, as proof of their innocence and the truth of their words. He meant, of course, to see his brother, for whom his soul longed. He carried out his word by imprisoning them for three days, to press them for the same purpose, which was repentance.

42.6.0.en: After disciplining them for three days in prison, they were very humbled and feared his vengeance against them. So he brought them out and spoke to them firmly but with more gentleness than before, and declared that he feared God, so he would not punish them more than their sin deserved, and that he would imprison only one of them as a pledge until they brought their youngest brother. He did not mean to torture them but only to discipline them, and he wanted to send them away with grain so that his father and the rest of his household might live, and so that they might bring Benjamin quickly.

42.7.0.en: Joseph's brothers began to feel their sins and said to one another in Hebrew that they had sinned against their brother Joseph. Reuben, the eldest brother, rebuked them because they had not listened to his word, for he had put Joseph in the pit so as to bring him out at a suitable time, whereas they wanted to kill him, then lessened their vengeance and sold him as a slave. Joseph was hearing and understanding, and they did not know it, because they spoke together in Hebrew, which they thought Joseph did not understand because he was an Egyptian who spoke the ancient Egyptian language, which is Coptic.

42.8.0.en: Joseph could not bear the humiliation of his brothers, so he withdrew to a private room and wept. This confirms his great love for them and that he did not want to take vengeance on them. Then he returned and pretended harshness, and bound Simeon before their eyes in order to frighten them, so that they would hasten to bring Benjamin. He chose Simeon in particular because of his cruelty and his sharp temper, which appeared in the killing of those who had violated his sister Dinah (ch. 34:25-29), so that this would give him a greater opportunity for repentance if he entered into affliction.

42.9.0.en: Sack: their bag, that is, their sack filled with grain.

42.9.1.en: Joseph commanded his servants to give them grain, so they filled their sacks and, without their knowledge, put the silver they had paid as the price of the grain inside their sacks. They thanked Joseph and went on their way back to Canaan in fear.

42.10.0.en: The inn: a place of lodging, like a small hotel on the road.

42.10.1.en: After they had spent a night on the road, one of them opened his sack in the morning to give his donkey fodder of grain, and he was surprised to find his silver in the sack. He told his brothers, and they were greatly amazed and bewildered, wondering what this blessing was that was with them.

42.11.0.en: Joseph's brothers reached their father Jacob in Canaan and told him what had happened: how the lord of Egypt had accused them of being spies, had investigated them and learned all their circumstances, and finally asked them to bring their youngest brother as proof of their innocence, and had imprisoned Simeon as a pledge until they should bring their brother.

42.12.0.en: When each one began to empty the grain that was in his sack, he was surprised to find his silver inside a bundle, and they were all amazed, they and their father.

42.13.0.en: Jacob was very sad because of what had happened to them in Egypt, because of the loss of Simeon, and because of their request to take Benjamin also, in addition to his loss of Joseph long ago.

42.14.0.en: Reuben came forward to his father to ask him to give him Benjamin, and he guaranteed his return to him by giving his own sons as a pledge: if Benjamin did not return, let Reuben's sons be killed. By this he meant to reassure Jacob, not to kill his sons but to give him a guarantee. But Jacob refused, fearing the loss of Benjamin, which would increase his sorrow so that he would die and go down to Sheol, to which all go, righteous and wicked, because redemption had not yet been accomplished. Perhaps he loved Benjamin more than the others because he was his youngest son and because of the loss of his brother Joseph, for he was what remained of the offspring of Rachel, his beloved wife.

42.14.1.en: God's blessings toward you are many. May you pay attention to them and thank God for them. Just as God gave each one his silver in his sack, He gives you blessings you do not expect, to bind your heart to Him, so do not be troubled by the afflictions that pass over you. The second meeting with Joseph

43.0.0.en: The famine increased in all the land of Canaan, and the grain that Jacob's sons had bought from Egypt ran out, so Jacob asked them to travel to Egypt to buy grain so that they would not die.

43.1.0.en: Judah answered his father that the lord of Egypt (Joseph) had said to them, you must bring your youngest brother with you the next time, otherwise I will not meet you or give you food.

43.2.0.en: Jacob reproached his sons for telling the lord of Egypt that they had a younger brother. They answered him that the man had asked them whether they had other brothers, and about their kindred and their father, and they did not know that he would ask them to bring this youngest brother.

43.3.0.en: Judah said to his father, give me Benjamin, and I guarantee that I will bring him back to you, otherwise I will be guilty in your sight all my life. He said this to encourage and reassure him, especially since it had become necessary for them to buy food, or else they and their children would perish. He also said to him, if we had obeyed the lord of Egypt and taken our brother, we could have gone and bought grain twice and not once only.

43.3.1.en: Try to reassure everyone who suffers from anxiety. Give him convincing proofs and words of encouragement, bear his anxiety, and pray for him until he calms down, and do not be annoyed with him, for you also are liable to be anxious like him.

43.4.1.en: Spices: a gum used in medicine.

43.4.2.en: Myrrh: a gum used in medicine.

43.4.3.en: Jacob was compelled to agree to take Benjamin with them, and he said to them, take with you a present of the finest of what the lands of Canaan produce, so that you may appease the lord of Egypt. He mentioned a group of the fruits of the land, some of which were discussed in (ch. 37:25).

43.5.0.en: He told them to take with them also the silver with which they would buy the new grain, together with the silver they had found in their sacks (ch. 42:35), and to take Benjamin with them. He prayed that God would keep them and that they would return with Simeon and Benjamin, and in surrender he said, but if I lose any of them, let the will of God be done.

43.6.0.en: Joseph's brothers arose, with Benjamin, the silver, and the present, and went to Egypt and met Joseph. When he saw them with Benjamin, he told the chief of his servants, the steward over his house, to bring them into his palace to eat with him, and he brought them in.

43.7.0.en: Joseph's brothers were afraid when he brought them into his palace, lest they be killed there because of the accusation of espionage or of stealing the silver, the price of the grain they had bought the previous time. So they explained to the steward of Joseph's house what had happened to them and how they had found their silver in their sacks, and that they had brought it with them, in addition to new silver to buy grain.

43.8.0.en: The steward of Joseph's house reassured them that their silver had reached him, and perhaps Joseph had instructed him to say that. Then he welcomed them, gave them water to wash their feet and water for their animals, and fulfilled for them the duties of hospitality, while they were astonished at what was happening to them and even afraid. So they prepared their present to offer to Joseph when he came, that he might be pleased with them and forgive them. And the steward of the house brought Simeon out to them to reassure them, and they rejoiced in him.

43.9.0.en: Joseph arrived at his house, and his brothers hurried to bow down before him and present their gift. He asked them about the welfare of their father, then inquired of them about Benjamin, whether he was their brother, and they answered yes, so he asked grace and blessing for him from God. Joseph could not bear to see Benjamin and speak with him, so he hurried to his chamber to weep there.

43.9.1.en: Let feelings of love toward others be what moves you in your dealings and conversations with them, even if you are sometimes firm with them or hide your feelings for a time in order to teach them something. But care for everyone and do not mention their sins and offenses.

43.10.0.en: Joseph washed his face and came out to meet his brothers at the table of food. He sat at a table of his own, as was the custom of the great men of Egypt, and his brothers sat at a table by themselves, and his Egyptian guests at another table, because it was the custom of the Egyptians not to eat with foreigners, either because of their sense of their own dignity or because of their aversion to foreign enemies such as the Hyksos.

43.10.1.en: Here Joseph is a type of Christ, who gives His Body and Blood to all the believers, whether of Jewish or Gentile origin.

43.11.0.en: Joseph seated his brothers according to the order of their ages, and they were greatly amazed at how he knew that. Then he honored them according to the Egyptian custom of honoring, by taking meats and foods from his table and giving each one of them, but he gave more to his brother Benjamin, for he gave him five times as much as his brothers. All this while his brothers were stunned at this extraordinary honor.

43.11.1.en: Each one of us has his blessed portion in Christ. Be careful to enjoy these spiritual blessings with which the Lord has favored you, and rejoice and thank Him for them always.

44.0.0.en: As much as they can carry: fill them abundantly, as much as they can be filled.

44.0.1.en: Joseph asked the chief of his servants to fill his brothers' sacks with grain abundantly and to return each one's silver inside each sack, for he loved them very much and wanted to honor them in every way.

44.1.1.en: Joseph could not bear to be parted from his brother Benjamin, so he wanted to keep him by putting his silver cup in Benjamin's sack, so that he could be seized and returned to Joseph on a charge of theft, and in order to test his brothers' feelings toward Benjamin, whether they would leave him in Egypt and return or hold fast to him, in addition to pressing them to complete their repentance.

44.1.2.en: Seek the repentance of those around you by every means, whether by encouragement or by alerting them to the passing away of the world, the seriousness of sin, or the hardness of judgment. Tell them of the beauty of life with God and the glories of heaven, and be persevering in order to bring them to Christ.

44.2.0.en: In the early morning Joseph's brothers took their sacks filled with grain and departed, and Joseph charged the steward of his house to pursue them and rebuke them for stealing his cup, which he prized, and he did as he had commanded him.

44.3.0.en: Joseph's brothers denounced this strange accusation of theft and defended themselves by saying that the silver they had found in their sacks they had returned to him, but he told them it was a blessing from their God, so how could they steal the cup of the lord of Egypt after he had honored them in his house. They judged that whoever was found with it should die, and that they all would become slaves to the lord of Egypt. They said this with confidence, being sure that they had not stolen from him.

44.4.0.en: The chief of Joseph's servants agreed to their words but lightened the judgment, so that the one with whom the cup was found would become a slave, he alone, and the rest would be innocent. He began to search their sacks from the eldest to the youngest, and he found the cup in Benjamin's sack. They were greatly distressed and expressed that by tearing their clothes, and they put their sacks on their animals and returned in deep humiliation, under arrest, to Joseph's house.

44.4.1.en: Thus they benefited from the affliction in which Joseph had placed them, for their feelings toward Benjamin became good, and each one did not selfishly think of his own interest, in addition to their feeling of their former sin toward Joseph.

44.5.0.en: When Joseph's brothers came in before him, they bowed down in fear and trembling because of the crime in which they had been caught, and he rebuked them for stealing his cup, by which he takes omens, whether this was true or merely a rebuke, since it was the custom of the Egyptians to hold to omens of good and ill.

44.6.0.en: Judah found no defense with which to justify them, so he declared that they were all slaves and subject to him.

44.7.0.en: Joseph said, I am just, so I will enslave only the one who did wrong and took the cup, that is, Benjamin, but as for you, you are free, so return to your homes.

44.8.0.en: Judah told Joseph everything that had happened in their conversation with their father, and his refusal to give them Benjamin because his heart was attached to him, for he was the son of his old age, and how Judah had guaranteed him. Judah begged Joseph to take him as a slave instead of Benjamin, because his father could not bear losing him and would die of deep sorrow, especially since he had lost the elder brother of Benjamin, born of his wife Rachel, whom he loved.

44.8.1.en: Thus Judah offered himself as a ransom for his brother Benjamin, and this is a declaration of the spiritual improvement of Judah and his brothers, their departure from selfishness, and their arrival at self-giving love after the example of Christ the Redeemer.

44.8.2.en: Look to the needs of those around you in order to offer them love, even at the expense of your comfort, and if you give much, know that by this you are a true disciple of your Christ and deserve a place with Him in heaven. Joseph reveals himself
